knowledge_point.title: Finding a General Solution in Implicit Form

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2 \cos{\left(y + 5 \right)}}{\left(x + 4\right) \tan{\left(y + 5 \right)}}$ for $\left(x+4\right)\ne 0$ and $-\frac{\pi }{2}<\left(y+5\right)<\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Also require $\left(y+5\right)\ne 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2 \cos{\left(y + 5 \right)}}{\left(x + 4\right) \tan{\left(y + 5 \right)}} \\ (\tan{\left(y + 5 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 5 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2}{x + 4}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\tan{\left(y + 5 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 5 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2}{x + 4})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y + 5 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 5 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (\frac{2}{x + 4})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y + 5 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 5 \right)})\,\text{d}y & =\int (\frac{2}{x + 4})\,\text{d}x \\ \sec{\left(y + 5 \right)} & =2 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 4}\right| \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\sec{\left(y + 5 \right)}=2 \ln{\left(\left|{x + 4}\right| \right)}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3 \cos{\left(y + 3 \right)}}{x \tan{\left(y + 3 \right)}}$ for $x\ne 0$ and $-\frac{\pi }{2}<\left(y+3\right)<\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Also require $\left(y+3\right)\ne 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3 \cos{\left(y + 3 \right)}}{x \tan{\left(y + 3 \right)}} \\ (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{3}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (\frac{3}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\tan{\left(y + 3 \right)} \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)})\,\text{d}y & =\int (\frac{3}{x})\,\text{d}x \\ \sec{\left(y + 3 \right)} & =3 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\sec{\left(y + 3 \right)}=3 \ln{\left(\left|{x}\right| \right)}+C.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\left(y + 5\right) \sin{\left(x + 1 \right)}$ for $\left(y+5\right)\ne 0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\left(y + 5\right) \sin{\left(x + 1 \right)} \\ (\frac{1}{y + 5})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sin{\left(x + 1 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{y + 5})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\sin{\left(x + 1 \right)})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\frac{1}{y + 5})\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int (\sin{\left(x + 1 \right)})\,\text{d}x \\ \int (\frac{1}{y + 5})\,\text{d}y & =\int (\sin{\left(x + 1 \right)})\,\text{d}x \\ \ln{\left(\left|{y + 5}\right| \right)} & =- \cos{\left(x + 1 \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
\ln{\left(\left|{y + 5}\right| \right)}=- \cos{\left(x + 1 \right)}+C.
$$
